*Endoscopy Technician Matthew Moreno reports OER-PRO | 2934613 displayed Error Code E05 during an automated cycle. No Connector Tubes were being used, but Connector jig (GN312400) was installed on the Tub Connector Ports. They pressed the Stop Button to quell the Code and called Olympus TAC for advice. 
*Using the OER-PRO Technical Guide and OER-PRO Operation Manual as my LM Reference Documents, I guided Matthew Moreno through troubleshooting. He observed that the Tub Fluid Level Sensor and Tub Float Sensor had intact Covers. He removed the covers, cleaned those Sensors with Iso-Alcohol and replaced the Covers. He observed that the Tub Float Sensor had free play and that when it was raised, it triggered the E05 Error Code to display again. He pressed the Stop Button to quell the Code He examined the Drain Port Mesh Filter Cover and Circulation Port Mesh Filter Cover and observed that they were clean and the ports unobstructed. He replaced them. He observed that the Drain Hose was not obstructed and draped correctly. OER-PRO | 2934613 shares a drain with another OER Unit, but that Unit was not in service at the time. No other OER units have displayed this Error Code. 
*I advised Matthew Moreno to call for another automated cycle. He will call TAC if there are further Error Codes.

22 JUL 2026 Sarah Barettino (TAC) 
OER-ELITE | 2201332 - E023 The air flush pressure and fluid feeding pressure are too high
Kitrell, endo tech calling in because OER is displaying E023. Prior to calling had changed air filter from previous error and power cycled unit. Error is persistent for multiple reprocessing attempts. No customer remedial actions available in OER-Elite technical guide. Dispatch requested. WO off to dispatch.

23 JUL 2026 - Paul White (FSE) Received case at 8:30am MST. Onsite tested the OER-Elite to confirm issue. Issue found to be E021 not E023. Confirmed the compressor was working and that there were no leaks in the unit. Lights on the CPU board not lighting up on the starting or stopping of the different pumps. Opened second Parts Request and ordered the CPU board and SSR to insure the completion of the repair.


28 JUL 2026 Ed McCawley (FSE): FSE arrived on site and a the FSE replaced the compressor that was ordered.  The FSE removed the old one and replaced it with the new compressor and ensured all of the connections and hose that were removed were put back in place and in good condition.  The FSE opened the maintenance tool an confirmed that the Compressor was working.  The FSE  ran program X and inspected the unit for any possible leaks and about 10 minutes in the machine alarmed an E023 error code.  The FSE used the maintenance tool to run the pressure sensor adjustment and when the pressure was checked it was at 1023.  The FSE adjusted the pressure in the range of 695 to 750  and ran the machine again. Program X was ran and the machine alarmed about 5 minutes in e021-3.  The FSE confirmed all of the tubing was firmly seated and there werent any air leaks.  The FSE ran an air purge and again the machine alarmed  e021-3  the FSE at that point got a new airfilter to confirm that there was not a problem with the existing filter.  The Air purge was ran again and the machine failed again.  The FSE went into the maintenance program again and tested the recovery valve and there was a noticeable audible click.  The FSE then tested the bypass valve to see if there was also an audible click and there was only a faint click which should be louder.  The FSE ordered the Bypass Valve and informed the customer of the findings and will come back the next day to replace the bypass valve.

30 JUL 2026 ? Ed McCawley (FSE) ? FSE arrived on customer site and replaced the bad bypass valve with a new one.  The FSE Then performed program X to confirm the unit was working properly.  The ubit passed the Program X test program and the Customer was made aware of the repair that was done and that they could use the unit for Patient care.  Completed test cycle successfully with no errors.  Performed repair per OER-Elite Technical Guide.  Equipment passed the electrical safety test with results attached.

31 JUL 2026 ? Ed McCawley (FSE) ? Labor time for today is for case closure and review for FSM

24 JUL 2026 Kevin Petridis (TAC Software):
Jessica Wolnowski (313-673-1635), Surgical Tech, called to report an E16 error on their OER-PRO (SN: 2633607). While discussing the issue, the nurse stated that the unit successfully completed two cycles yesterday, but the error occurred today.

I instructed the customer to inspect both gas filters, and she confirmed that both were dry. I then advised her to clean the fluid and float level sensor; however, she stated that this component is cleaned daily as part of their routine maintenance.

Next, I instructed her to run a test cycle. As soon as she pressed Start, the unit immediately generated an E12 error.

Based on the troubleshooting performed, I advised the customer that an FSE dispatch would be required. The customer verified the service contact information and confirmed that billing should be directed to the facility.

29 JUL 2026 - Andrew Presas (FSE) - FSE arrived on site and opened the side panels of the unit. It was observed that the disinfectant tank was only 1/3 full. Customer the indicated that they stopped the cycle when basin was full. It was determined that the basin was drained down the drain rather than back into the tank leading to the low level in the tank. FSE drained the rest of the LCG from the tank and then filled it with water. FSE marked the level inside the tank once it was full. FSE ran 2 cycles and observed that the level in the tank reached the mark when recirculated. FSE loaded new LCG into the tank and ran 2 more cycles to ensure that the unit was operating as expected. After 4 cycles completed successfully and the error was not replicated the unit was returned to the customer.

Completed test cycle successfully with no errors.  Performed repair per OER-Pro Technical Guide.

FSE informed the customer and immediately provided a quote for the replacement hose. Since a replacement hose was available in FSE trunk stock, FSE replaced it during the same visit.

FSE ran the OER Pro through several cycles and confirmed that the unit was operating properly with no further E16 errors or leaks.

Repair was performed in accordance with the OER Pro Technical Guide. The equipment passed the electrical safety test, with the results attached.
